batching.loss_reduction: chemkan.losses.trajectory_mse, UNCHANGED: mean over species, sum over observation times, then MEAN over the trajectories in the batch. A batch of k trajectories divides by k, so a batch of one divides by one.
batching.epoch_metric: total_loss/mse_loss is the FULL 20-trajectory Eq. 18 metric evaluated under no_grad at the parameter state the epoch STARTS from -- the identical definition and the identical parameter state the unbatched trainer logs, so the column is directly comparable across batch sizes. It is NOT the last mini-batch's loss. The sample-weighted mean of the batch losses actually optimized during the epoch is logged separately as batch_loss_running_mean; those are measured at different parameter states within the epoch and are a running quantity, not the epoch metric.
batching.epoch_definition: one epoch is one complete pass over all training trajectories, each visited exactly once. An epoch is never redefined as an optimizer step.

in_training_evaluation.parameter_state: before this epoch's optimizer update -- the same state that produced the epoch's training loss
in_training_evaluation.normalizer: train-only min-max (never refit on test data)
